answer: Path Diversity Flow Routing calculates the independent topological paths between network nodes to throttle untrusted clusters. A newly joined agent node must route traffic across an uneven ridge of sparse graph connections to reach critical resources. If traffic volume exceeds the disjoint path capacity, packets drop automatically. The attacker pays a heavy computational and latency cost because duplicating nodes multiplies edge congestion on every basalt gateway, forcing sybil operators to provision actual routing hardware instead of cheap virtual identities akin to a digital sonnet.
